question.worked_solution:
We start by recalling the conversion table for mass units. 

| Name | Symbol | Conversion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kilogram | $\text{kg}$ | $1\,\text{kg}=1\,000\,\text{g}$ |
| Gram | $\text{g}$ | Base Unit |
| Milligram | $\text{mg}$ | $1\,000\,\text{mg}=1\,\text{g}$ |

$$

$$

There are $1000\,\text{mg}$ per $\text{g},$ which we can write as follows:

$$
\frac{1000\,\text{mg}}{\text{g}}
$$

This is our conversion factor.

Now, multiplying $1.2\,\text{g}$ by our conversion factor, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1.2\,\text{g} & =1.2\,\text{g}\cdot \frac{1\,000\,\text{mg}}{\text{g}} \\  & =1.2\,\cancel{\text{g}}\cdot \frac{1\,000\,\text{mg}}{\cancel{\text{g}}} \\  & =1.2\cdot 1\,000\,\text{mg} \\  & =1\,200\,\text{mg}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $1.2\,\text{g}$ is equivalent to $1\,200\,\text{mg}.$
